narrative.overview:
The landing page is INSTALL.md with the product as step 0. It reads top to bottom in the order a host proceeds: what you get (the workspace itself, operable), what you need, the deploy, becoming the host, inviting people, what it costs. The wordmark band carries the sentence and the single action; nothing on the page is arranged the way the category arranges it. There is no hero slogan, no feature cards, no pricing grid, no logo wall, and the offer is never hidden behind the product.

The world is Lounge, the app's own, borrowed whole: warm cream page, sand sidebar, terracotta accent for the one action and for links, the dark stage only inside call surfaces, live green for presence, ID-derived person hues, IBM Plex everywhere. The site's own layer is typographic and structural rather than chromatic: IBM Plex set large with tight tracking for numbered step headings, hairline rows in place of cards, and a frame only where the page shows something (the workspace, the person's terminal while their agent follows INSTALL.md, an app screen). With all content removed the page is a cream ground, one terracotta word, hairlines and one dark rectangle.

Density is generous between steps and app-dense inside the exhibits, because the exhibit is the app at its real 15px base rather than a picture of it. Light and dark come from the same tokens, resolved by `data-theme` or `prefers-color-scheme` exactly as in the app. Confirmed rejections: Discord marketing tells (blurple, mascots, character illustration), startup chrome (gradient blobs, glass cards, badge rows, logo walls, floating or 3D screenshots), fabricated proof, display faces and shipped rasters.
keyCharacteristics: Tokens are consumed from the app's theme (`@vaskel/ui/theme.css`), never redefined; the site adds one colour (`terminal`).
One filled accent control on the page (Deploy your own); every other control is hairline-and-surface, plain text, or ink-filled.
Step headings read `N · Title` in IBM Plex Sans at clamp(2rem, 1.2rem + 2.6vw, 3rem), 700, -0.03em, the numeral in muted.
Hairline rows, not cards; 12px frames with the row shadow are reserved for exhibits.
The dark stage and its gold appear only inside call surfaces (Happening-now card, pinned bar, picture-in-picture window, stage, shared terminal) and the agent console.
Exhibits are DOM built from the app's components, operable and localized through the four real catalogs in the visitor's browser language; no raster ships.
Light and dark from the same tokens, with `data-theme` and `prefers-color-scheme` as in the app.

rules.name: The Borrowed Palette Rule
rules.body: site.css declares no colour literal; every colour is a `var(--color-*)` from the app's theme, and the site's only addition is `terminal`. A colour the app does not have is a colour the site does not have.

rules.name: The One Filled Action Rule
rules.body: Outside the exhibits, exactly one control on the page is filled with `accent`: Deploy your own in the wordmark band. Everything else is surface-and-hairline, plain text, or ink-filled.

rules.name: The Stage Stays Inside the Call Rule
rules.body: `stage` and `stage-accent` appear only on call surfaces and on screens (the shared terminal, the agent console). The page never sets a dark band or section; dark on the cream page means a call is happening or a terminal is open.

rules.name: The One Family Set Large Rule
rules.body: Type contrast comes from size, weight and tracking of IBM Plex, never from a second family. Tracking tightens as size grows (-0.02em at 1.1rem, -0.03em at display, -0.06em on the wordmark) and is zeroed under CJK languages.

rules.name: The Numbered Heading Rule
rules.body: Every step heading is `N · Title`: the numeral and the middle dot in muted at 600 tabular, the title in ink. The sequence starts at 0 with the product itself. Headings carry no eyebrow or kicker above them.

rules.name: The Row Shadow Rule
rules.body: Page chrome lifts by at most the row shadow; the popover shadow belongs to things that float over content. No shadow is invented on the site.

dos: Do consume `@vaskel/ui` unchanged (theme, base, components and timeline) under the app's own token names; add a site token only for something the app has no word for, as `terminal` was.
Do keep one filled `accent` control per page and hairline-and-surface for the rest.
Do number every step heading `N · Title` at the display style, numeral in muted tabular, with no eyebrow above it.
Do lay lists out as hairline rows and reserve 12px frames with the row shadow for exhibits (the workspace, the agent console, an app screen).
Do build exhibits from the app's own components in DOM, localized through the four catalogs with `lang` set on the exhibit from the visitor's browser; ship no raster.
Do keep the dark stage, its gold and the popover shadow inside call surfaces and screens; the agent console is a screen.
Do keep the 15px root, the 16px gutter, the 1408px cap, the 40rem measure and the 640px / 900px breakpoints.
Do set every number that lines up (costs, times, counts, step numerals) in tabular numerals.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: transitions collapse to 0.01ms and scripted motion does not run; the still frame is complete.
donts: Don't load a display face or a second family; Plex at display size is the identity.
Don't introduce Discord marketing tells: blurple, mascots, character illustration.
Don't add startup chrome: gradient blobs, glass cards, badge rows, logo walls, floating or 3D screenshots.
Don't add proof surfaces (testimonial cards, member counts, uptime, benchmarks); cost figures come only from docs/cost-scenarios.json.
Don't put a dark band or section on the page; dark means a call surface or a terminal.
Don't invent a shadow, a radius or a colour literal in site.css; the app's three shadows, its radius scale and its tokens are the vocabulary.
Don't restyle the app's components inside an exhibit; the exhibit is proof because it is the app's geometry.
Don't letter-space or uppercase under zh-Hant, zh-Hans or ja.
